topic.title: Learning to Rank from Noisy Preferences
topic.overview: Ranking converts incomplete comparisons into an ordering of items, documents, or models. This topic studies how to learn preference functions, choose informative comparisons, optimize ranking metrics, and quantify uncertainty. Pairwise judgments need not be perfectly consistent, so recovering an ordering involves both statistical modeling and combinatorial choices.
topic.whyItMatters: A leaderboard or retrieval list can appear definitive even when supported by sparse, noisy, or context-dependent preferences. Reliable ranking methods should expose uncertainty and allocate comparison budgets carefully. The appropriate objective may prioritize the best few items rather than agreement across every possible pair.
topic.evolution: A 1997 approach separates preference learning from approximate ordering. Later work studies ranking metrics, pairwise sample efficiency, and active elicitation under probabilistic models. In 2026, DMLRank uses debiased machine learning to estimate flexible ranking scores from human preferences, accommodate ties, and inform budget-constrained collection of additional comparisons.
openQuestions: How should ranking uncertainty be communicated when adjacent items are statistically indistinguishable?
Which comparison policies remain informative when preferences vary across users or contexts?

papers.title: Sorting with Predictions
papers.tldr: Prediction-assisted sorting algorithms use fewer exact comparisons when predictions are good and degrade smoothly as prediction errors grow.

papers.title: Identifiability Matters: Revealing the Hidden Recoverable Condition in Unbiased Learning to Rank
papers.tldr: The paper characterizes relevance recovery through graph connectivity and proposes dataset interventions for otherwise unidentifiable ranking problems.

papers.title: An Analysis of Elo Rating Systems via Markov Chains
papers.tldr: A Markov chain analysis shows that Elo learns skill parameters at a competitive rate under the Bradley–Terry–Luce model and informs tournament design.

papers.title: Computerized Adaptive Testing via Collaborative Ranking
papers.tldr: CCAT uses other students as reference anchors to improve the consistency between adaptive-test rankings and underlying student abilities.

papers.title: Prediction-Powered Ranking of Large Language Models
papers.tldr: The framework combines human and automated comparisons to produce language-model rank sets with asymptotic coverage guarantees.

papers.title: Comparing Few to Rank Many: Active Human Preference Learning Using Randomized Frank-Wolfe Method
papers.tldr: A randomized optimization algorithm efficiently selects informative item comparisons to improve preference rankings under a limited feedback budget.

papers.title: LapSum - One Method to Differentiate Them All: Ranking, Sorting and Top-k Selection
papers.tldr: LapSum provides a shared, efficient construction for differentiable ranking, top-k selection, and permutations.

papers.title: Ranking with Multiple Oracles: From Weak to Strong Stochastic Transitivity
papers.tldr: Two algorithms efficiently rank items using multiple noisy oracles, with theoretical guarantees under weak and strong stochastic transitivity.

papers.title: Active Seriation: Efficient Ordering Recovery with Statistical Guarantees
papers.tldr: An active algorithm recovers hidden item orderings from noisy similarity queries with optimal statistical guarantees.

papers.title: AcuRank: Uncertainty-Aware Adaptive Computation for Listwise Reranking
papers.tldr: AcuRank directs reranking computation toward uncertain document relevance decisions, improving the measured accuracy–efficiency trade-off.

papers.title: Median Selection with Noisy and Structural Information
papers.tldr: Noisy comparison predictions and partial ordering information can reduce the costly exact comparisons needed for median selection.

papers.title: Preference-Based Dynamic Ranking Structure Recognition
papers.tldr: The framework identifies evolving ranking groups and structural changes in preference data, with consistency results and uncertainty estimates.

papers.title: BlitzRank: Principled Zero-shot Ranking Agents with Tournament Graphs
papers.tldr: BlitzRank reuses comparison information through tournament graphs to deliver competitive document rankings with substantially fewer tokens.

papers.title: Calibrated Preference Learning: The Case of Label Ranking
papers.tldr: The paper formalizes several distinct forms of ranking calibration and shows that accuracy alone does not fully capture them.

papers.title: Contrastive Order Learning: A General Framework for Ordinal Regression
papers.tldr: ConOrd uses rank-sensitive contrastive comparisons across training batches to improve ordinal regression across age and visual quality tasks.

papers.title: Fairness in Aggregation: Optimal Top-$k$ and Improved Full Ranking
papers.tldr: The paper gives an optimal fair top-k aggregation algorithm and improves fair full-ranking approximation from a factor of three to two.

papers.title: Learning to Rank by Directly Optimizing Full-Order Probabilities
papers.tldr: The Full-Order Bound makes whole-list ranking probabilities tractable to optimize and improves full-order metrics in experiments.

papers.title: Learning to Rank from Incomplete Rankings
papers.tldr: PIRATE learns top-ranked items under a broader model of incomplete feedback while retaining near-optimal sample-complexity guarantees.

papers.title: Nonparametric LLM Evaluation from Preference Data
papers.tldr: DMLRank combines flexible preference modeling with statistically grounded ranking estimates and budget-aware preference collection.

papers.title: Relevance-Based Embeddings: Lightweight Candidate Retrieval via Heavy-Ranker Calls
papers.tldr: Relevance profiles against support queries and items turn expensive ranking scores into embeddings for lightweight candidate retrieval.

papers.title: Stochastic Order Learning: An Approach to Rank Estimation Using Noisy Data
papers.tldr: SOL models noisy ordinal labels as multiple plausible ranks and learns representations that preserve probabilistic ordering relationships.
